title: Full faithfulness from final comma comparisons in a coherent square
statement:
Use small quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces, equivalences and colimiting coherent cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] in a fixed universe, enlarging the universe for functor categories. Let $A,B,X,Y$ be small quasicategories, $i:A\to B$, $q:A\to X$, $r:B\to Y$, $u:X\to Y$ coherent functors, and $\theta:r i\simeq u q$ a coherent natural equivalence. Assume $i$ is fully faithful and $q$ is essentially surjective, meaning that each object of $X$ is equivalent to $q(a)$ for some $a\in A$. For each $a\in A$ form the induced coherent comma functor
$$T_a:(q\downarrow q(a))\longrightarrow(r\downarrow u q(a)),\qquad(b,\alpha:q(b)\to q(a))\longmapsto(i(b),u(\alpha)\theta_b).$$
The comma category $(v\downarrow z)$ for $v:K\to Z$ is the simplicial pullback
$$K\times_{Z,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Z)\times_{Z,\operatorname{ev}_1}\{z\},$$
so it retains all triangle homotopies and higher simplices. Suppose every $T_a$ is final: restriction carries each colimiting coherent cocone on each diagram into any quasicategory to a colimiting cocone with the same apex. Then $u$ is fully faithful: for every $x,x'\in X$ the map
$$\operatorname{Map}_X(x,x')\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_Y(u(x),u(x'))$$
is an equivalence of spaces.

source.place: The general square argument in the proof of Theorem 7.5.18, printed p. 380 (PDF p. 395); its inputs are Proposition 6.1.14, Proposition 6.1.15 and pointwise Kan extension in Proposition 6.4.9 with finality Theorem 6.4.5. This general form abstracts the proof, not the Brown theorem. No Stacks tag states it. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $a,a'\in A$ and write $I=(q\downarrow q(a'))$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-comma-corepresentable-colimit] with $K=A$, $Z=X$, $v=q$, $k=a$, $z=q(a')$. It gives a colimiting coherent cocone on $D:I\to\mathcal S$, $D(b,\alpha)=\operatorname{Map}_A(a,b)$, whose apex is $M=\operatorname{Map}_X(q(a),q(a'))$ and whose leg is $f\mapsto\alpha\circ q(f)$. No Kan extension of an arbitrary diagram or generation assertion is being assumed.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.14 applied to opposite categories, and the colimit dual of Proposition 6.4.9: pointwise Kan extension on a covariant corepresentable.

proof.text: Put $J=(r\downarrow u q(a'))$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-comma-corepresentable-colimit] with $K=B$, $Z=Y$, $v=r$, $k=i(a)$ and $z=u q(a')$. The diagram $E:J\to\mathcal S$, $E(c,\beta)=\operatorname{Map}_B(i(a),c)$, has the colimiting cocone with apex $N=\operatorname{Map}_Y(r i(a),u q(a'))$ and legs $g\mapsto\beta\circ r(g)$. By the finality hypothesis on $T_{a'}$, restriction of this very cocone to $I$ is still colimiting, with legs $g\mapsto u(\alpha)\circ\theta_b\circ r(g)$ on $E T_{a'}(b,\alpha)=\operatorname{Map}_B(i(a),i(b))$. Here finality is the assumed preservation of colimiting coherent cocones under restriction.

source.place: Corollary 7.5.17 proof: restrict the pointwise comma-colimit cocone along the final comparison, specialized to the covariant corepresentable at i(a).

proof.text: The coherent Hom-functor transformation induced by $i$ restricts to $e:D\to E T_{a'}$, with component $\operatorname{Map}_A(a,b)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(i(a),i(b))$. Every component is an equivalence by full faithfulness of $i$, so [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes $e$ an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal S)$. Precomposition with $e$ identifies the spaces of cocones from these two diagrams into every constant diagram. Thus the colimit mapping-space criterion in that node shows that the cocone of Step 2 composed with $e$ is colimiting on $D$. Its apex is $N$ and its leg is $f\mapsto u(\alpha)\circ\theta_b\circ r i(f)$.

source.place: The first equivalence in the proof of Theorem 7.5.18, specialized to a corepresentable; objectwise full faithfulness identifies the restricted coherent diagrams.

proof.text:
Consider the actual map $w:M\to N$, $\gamma\mapsto u(\gamma)\circ\theta_a$. It is a morphism between the cocone of Step 1 and the cocone of Step 3: on the leg at $(b,\alpha)$, naturality of $\theta:r i\simeq u q$ gives
$$u(\alpha)\circ\theta_b\circ r i(f)\simeq u(\alpha)\circ u q(f)\circ\theta_a\simeq u(\alpha\circ q(f))\circ\theta_a.$$
These are coherent identifications of transformations, including all parameters, because $\theta$ is a coherent natural equivalence and the Hom bifunctor preserves the functorial composition coherences. Both cocones are initial objects of the cocone quasicategory by Steps 1 and 3. Its full subcategory of initial objects is a Kan complex by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so this cocone morphism, and hence its apex map $w$, is an equivalence. Precomposition with $\theta_a$ is an equivalence of mapping spaces: its inverse is precomposition with an inverse of $\theta_a$, and the two inverse homotopies follow from its inverse triangles and associativity and unit homotopies. Since $w$ is the composite of $u_*:M\to\operatorname{Map}_Y(u q(a),u q(a'))$ with this equivalence, $u_*$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Theorem 7.5.18 proof, evaluated on covariant corepresentables; the displayed identity verifies the actual comparison map, rather than merely identifying two abstract apices.

proof.text: For arbitrary $x,x'\in X$, essential surjectivity provides $a,a'\in A$ and equivalences $s:q(a)\to x$ and $t:q(a')\to x'$. The map $\operatorname{Map}_X(x,x')\to\operatorname{Map}_X(q(a),q(a'))$ given by $f\mapsto t^{-1}\circ f\circ s$ is an equivalence, with inverse $g\mapsto t\circ g\circ s^{-1}$. Their composites are homotopic to the identities by the inverse triangles, associativity and unitality of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Applying $u$ gives the corresponding equivalence between $\operatorname{Map}_Y(u(x),u(x'))$ and $\operatorname{Map}_Y(u q(a),u q(a'))$. Coherent Hom functoriality identifies the two composites around the square, since $u(t^{-1}\circ f\circ s)\simeq u(t)^{-1}\circ u(f)\circ u(s)$. Its bottom map is the equivalence of Step 4, and its two vertical maps are equivalences, so its top map is an equivalence. This is full faithfulness of $u$. If $A$ is empty, essential surjectivity makes $X$ empty and there are no pairs to check.

source.place: Theorem 7.5.18 proof, reduction to representables in the essential image of the left functor, and Proposition 6.1.15(ii); explicit extension from q-images by conjugation with equivalences.
